items.text: You might have mixed feelings about rain.
For those experiencing long periods of drought, rain can bring joy.
But for those wanting to enjoy the outdoors, a large downpour can ruin the experience.
Getting drenched by the weather can make you feel cold and weaken your immune system, but there are some surprising benefits to going out in the rain, provided you've got your brolly and raincoat!

level1.label: 条件状语从句
level1.text: provided you've got your brolly and raincoat

items.text: Have you ever noticed a difference in the smell in the air after it's rained?

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: a difference in the smell in the air after it's rained

items.text: That smell has a name - petrichor.
This earthy scent, a pleasant one to many, happens when raindrops release particles from the ground.

level1.label: 时间状语从句
level1.text: when raindrops release particles from the ground

items.text: Humans are incredibly sensitive to the smell, which some scientists think is because it tells us there is new, fresh water.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: incredibly sensitive to the smell, which some scientists think is because it tells us there is new, fresh water

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: which some scientists think is because it tells us there is new, fresh water

items.text: It probably made our ancestors feel safe and calm.
And then there's the relaxing sound of raindrops splattering on a hard surface.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: the relaxing sound of raindrops splattering on a hard surface

items.text: A 2018 study published in PubMed Central by Thoma and colleagues found that the sound of rain can reduce the stress hormone cortisol and bring a sense of calm.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: A 2018 study published in PubMed Central by Thoma and colleagues

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that the sound of rain can reduce the stress hormone cortisol and bring a sense of calm

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: published in PubMed Central by Thoma and colleagues

items.text: When raindrops hit a hard surface, something called 'negative ions' are released into the air, which, when in high levels, are known to boost serotonin in the brain, again making us feel more relaxed.

level1.label: 时间状语从句
level1.text: When raindrops hit a hard surface

level1.label: 定语从句
level1.text: which, when in high levels, are known to boost serotonin in the brain

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: again making us feel more relaxed

items.text: However, there isn't a scientific consensus about exactly how this is happening.
These negative ions also make the air cleaner.

Pam Dalton, a cognitive scientist at the Monell Chemical Senses Center in Pennsylvania, says there is reasonably good evidence that "the negative ions can clear dust, bacteria, allergens, and other particles from air, which for many can have a positive effect on respiratory health."

level1.label: 同位语
level1.text: a cognitive scientist at the Monell Chemical Senses Center in Pennsylvania

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: there is reasonably good evidence that "the negative ions can clear dust, bacteria, allergens, and other particles from air, which for many can have a positive effect on respiratory health."

level2.text: that "the negative ions can clear dust, bacteria, allergens, and other particles from air

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: which for many can have a positive effect on respiratory health.

items.text: The heavier the rain, the greater effect it has on cleaning the air.
You could feel some of these benefits from the comfort of your own home, just by opening the window and taking a whiff of the petrichor scent or listening to the pitter-patter sound on your roof.
Or, after making sure you're dressed in the right attire, step outside in the rain to fully experience the mood-boosting effects of those mysterious negative ions in the air.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: to fully experience the mood-boosting effects of those mysterious negative ions in the air

items.text: Just remember to come straight back inside if you see lightning, as this could be dangerous.
